===2017 season===
After going undrafted in the [[2017 NFL draft]], Jarwin signed with the [[Dallas Cowboys]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 12, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 12, 2017 |title=Cowboys Officially Sign 13 Rookie Free Agents Leading Into Rookie Minicamp |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-officially-sign-13-rookie-free-agents-leading-into-rookie-minicam-432126 |access-date=November 6, 2017 |website=DallasCowboys.com}}</ref> He was waived on September 2,<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 2, 2017 |title=Cowboys Make 38 Moves, One Trade To Reach 53; Kellen Moore Released |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-make-38-moves-one-trade-to-reach-53-kellen-moore-released-439246 |access-date=November 6, 2017 |website=DallasCowboys.com}}</ref> but was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 3, 2017 |title=Showers, Drafted CB & 2 WRs Headline Cowboys' 10-Man Practice Squad |url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2017/09/03/showers-drafted-cb-2-wrs-headline-cowboys%E2%80%99-10-man-practice-squad |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316061544/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2017/09/03/showers-drafted-cb-2-wrs-headline-cowboys%E2%80%99-10-man-practice-squad |archive-date=March 16, 2018 |access-date=November 6, 2017 |website=DallasCowboys.com}}</ref>

On October 26, 2017, Jarwin was promoted to the active roster, in order to avoid the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] signing him. The move forced the Cowboys to keep four [[tight end]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 26, 2017 |title=Cowboys Release QB Kellen Moore, Sign TE Blake Jarwin Off Practice Squad |url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2017/10/26/cowboys-release-qb-kellen-moore-sign-te-blake-jarwin-practice-squad |access-date=November 6, 2017 |website=DallasCowboys.com}}</ref> Jarwin appeared in only one game in his rookie year and recorded no statistics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Jarwin 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JarwBl00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=June 5, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2018 season===
With the unexpected retirements of starter [[Jason Witten]] and backup [[James Hanna (American football)|James Hanna]], Jarwin had a chance to compete for the starting tight end position, but was named the backup behind [[Geoff Swaim]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zucker |first=Joseph |date=April 27, 2018 |title=Jason Witten Reportedly Plans to Retire, Join ESPN's Monday Night Football Crew |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2619087-jason-witten-reportedly-plans-to-retire-join-espns-monday-night-football-crew |access-date=June 5, 2020 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=April 20, 2018 |title=Cowboys TE James Hanna retiring after battling knee injury |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2018/04/20/cowboys-te-james-hanna-retiring-after-battling-knee-injury/34094439/ |access-date=June 5, 2020 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

After Swaim was lost to an injury in Week 11, rookie [[Dalton Schultz]] passed Jarwin on the depth chart as the starter and was used mostly for blocking purposes. During the regular-season finale against the [[New York Giants]], Jarwin had the best game of his career, catching seven passes for 119 yards and three touchdowns in a narrow 36–35 road victory.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at New York Giants – December 30th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201812300nyg.htm |access-date=February 8, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Jarwin became the sixth tight end in franchise history to post a 100-yard receiving game and was named the NFC Offensive Player of the Week for his spectacular performance.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maya |first=Adam |date=January 2, 2019 |title=Josh Allen, Darius Leonard among Players of the Week |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001006931/article/josh-allen-darius-leonard-among-players-of-the-week |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190102193427/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001006931/article/josh-allen-darius-leonard-among-players-of-the-week |archive-date=January 2, 2019 |access-date=June 5, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Jarwin was named the starter for four games when the Cowboys used multiple tight end sets, finishing his second professional season with 27 receptions for 307 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Jarwin 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JarwBl00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=January 16, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2019 season===
In 2019, although Swaim left via [[free agency]], Witten returned to play professional football after spending the previous season as a ''[[Monday Night Football]]'' commentator.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teope |first=Herbie |date=February 28, 2019 |title=Jason Witten ends retirement, will return to Cowboys |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/jason-witten-ends-retirement-will-return-to-cowboys-0ap3000001019291?campaign=sf:fanshare:facebook |access-date=June 5, 2020 |website=[[NFL.com]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Jarwin was a backup at tight end behind Witten, posting 31 receptions for 365 yards and three touchdowns. Jarwin had a chance to start in seven contests, when the team opened the game in a two tight end formation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Jarwin 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JarwBl00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=June 5, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2020 season===
On March 16, 2020, Jarwin signed a three-year, $24.25 million contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=March 16, 2020 |title=Cowboys bring back TE Blake Jarwin on $24.25M deal |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/cowboys-bring-back-te-blake-jarwin-on-24-25m-deal-0ap3000001106451 |access-date=2021-09-12 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> The following day, it was announced in the media that Witten would be leaving the Cowboys to sign with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]], making Jarwin the starter at tight end.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldberg |first=Rob |date=March 17, 2020 |title=Ex-Cowboys TE Jason Witten, Raiders Reportedly Agree to 1-Year Contract |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2869320-ex-cowboys-te-jason-witten-raiders-reportedly-agree-to-contract |access-date=2021-09-12 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref>

During the season opener against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Jarwin recorded a 12-yard reception in the first half before leaving the eventual 20–17 road loss with a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at Los Angeles Rams – September 13th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009130ram.htm |access-date=February 8, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The next day, it was announced that he would be out for the season to undergo [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) surgery and was placed on [[injured reserve]] on September 15.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Epstein |first=Jori |date=September 14, 2020 |title=Dallas Cowboys lose starting LB Leighton Vander Esch for 6-8 weeks, TE Blake Jarwin for season |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/cowboys/2020/09/14/dallas-cowboys-injuries-leighton-vander-esch-blake-jarwin/5794221002/ |access-date=September 14, 2020 |website=USA TODAY}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Helman |first=David |date=September 14, 2020 |title=Blake Jarwin Expected To Have ACL Surgery |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/blake-jarwin-expected-to-have-acl-surgery |access-date=September 14, 2020 |website=www.dallascowboys.com}}</ref> He was replaced with Schultz in the starting lineup.

===2021 season===
Jarwin returned as the backup to Schultz. He suffered a career-threatening hip injury in the seventh game against the [[Minnesota Vikings]] and was placed on injured reserve on November 6, 2021.<ref name="o298">{{cite web |last=Halprin |first=David |date=2021-11-06 |title=Cowboys roster moves: Blake Jarwin to injured reserve, Francis Bernard activated |url=https://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2021/11/6/22767225/cowboys-roster-moves-blake-jarwin-to-injured-reserve-francis-bernard-activated |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=Blogging The Boys|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref>

Jarwin was activated on January 8, 2022. He played in the regular-season finale against the Eagles and the Wild Card playoff loss to the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. Jarwin finished the 2021 season with 11 receptions for 96 yards and two touchdowns in eight games and five starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Jarwin 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JarwBl00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=January 24, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 11, 2022, Jarwin was released after not being able to recover his previous form.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Helman |first=David |date=March 11, 2022 |title=Cowboys Release Veteran TE Blake Jarwin |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-release-veteran-te-blake-jarwin |access-date=2025-01-08 |website=DallasCowboys.com}}</ref>

'''Blake Jackson''' (born March 7, 1994) is an American [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] for the [[St. Louis Battlehawks]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL). He played college football at [[University of Mary Hardin–Baylor|Mary Hardin–Baylor]]. Jackson has also been a member of the [[Calgary Stampeders]], [[Cleveland Browns]], [[Houston Roughnecks (2020)|Houston Roughnecks]], [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]], and [[Seattle Sea Dragons]].

==College career==
Jackson played [[quarterback]] for [[University of Mary Hardin–Baylor|Mary Hardin–Baylor]]. He was D3 All-American, ASC Offensive player of the year, and National Championship MVP. He finished his senior season at Mary Hardin–Baylor with over 3,500 yds passing with 36 TDs, and over 1100 yards rushing with 12 TDs.

==Professional career==
===Calgary Stampeders===
After going undrafted in the [[2018 NFL draft]], Jackson signed with the [[Calgary Stampeders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) on April 23, 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |date=April 23, 2018 |title=Blake Jackson and Keith Reineke sign with CFL |publisher=CRUAthletics.com |url=https://cruathletics.com/news/2018/4/23/football-blake-jackson-and-keith-reineke-sign-with-cfl.aspx}}</ref> He was released by the Stampeders at the conclusion of training camp.

===Cleveland Browns===
After attending [[The Spring League]] Showcase in La Jolla, California in July 2018, Jackson signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]] as a [[wide receiver]] on July 27, 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 27, 2018 |title=Browns sign DL Zaycoven Henderson, WR Blake Jackson |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-dl-zaycoven-henderson-wr-blake-jackson}}</ref> He was waived by the Browns on September 1, 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gribble |first=Andrew |date=September 1, 2018 |title=Browns announce 53-man roster |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-announce-53-man-roster}}</ref> The Browns re-signed Jackson to their practice squad on October 16, 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 16, 2018 |title=Browns elevate WR Da'Mari Scott, LB Xavier Woodson-Luster to active roster |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-elevate-wr-da-mari-scott-lb-xavier-woodson-luster-to-active-roster}}</ref> Jackson was promoted to the Browns' active 53-man roster on December 28, 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |date=December 28, 2018 |title=Browns elevate WR Blake Jackson to active roster |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-elevate-wr-blake-jackson-to-active-roster}}</ref> 

Jackson was waived with an injury designation on August 2, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 2, 2019 |title=Browns sign TE Mik'Quan Deane |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-te-mik-quan-deane |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref> After clearing waivers, he was placed on the Browns' injured reserve list. He was later released with an injury settlement.

===Houston Roughnecks===
In October 2019, Jackson was selected by the [[Houston Roughnecks (2020)|Houston Roughnecks]] in the [[2020 XFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Talbot |first=Damond |date=October 16, 2019 |title=XFL Draft Phase 5: The Final Rounds of the Draft, Find out who was selected |url=https://www.nfldraftdiamonds.com/2019/10/xfl-draft-8/ |access-date=October 22, 2019 |publisher=NFL Draft Diamonds}}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Condotta |first=Bob |date=April 10, 2020 |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |work=SeattleTimes.com |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |access-date=July 17, 2020}}</ref> He played in five games for the Roughnecks, catching five passes for 50 yards and one touchdown.

===Winnipeg Blue Bombers===
Jackson signed with the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) on February 25, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Blue Bombers add Blake Jackson and Prince Robinson to roster |url=https://www.bluebombers.com/2021/02/25/blue-bombers-add-blake-jackson-prince-robinson-roster/ |website=BlueBombers.com |date=February 25, 2021 |access-date=February 25, 2021}}</ref> Jackson was having a promising training camp with the club in [[2021 Winnipeg Blue Bombers season|2021]] prior to suffering a season ending injury. He re-signed with the Blue Bombers on January 6, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-06|title=Blue Bombers sign receiver Blake Jackson|url=https://www.bluebombers.com/2022/01/06/blue-bombers-sign-receiver-blake-jackson/|access-date=2022-01-06|website=Winnipeg Blue Bombers|language=en}}</ref>

=== Seattle Sea Dragons ===
On November 17, 2022, Jackson was drafted by the [[Seattle Sea Dragons]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-18 |title=Rosters for all eight XFL teams: Full draft results and where Vic Beasley, Martavis Bryant landed |url=https://www.espn.com/xfl/story/_/id/35053464/xfl-draft-results-2023-full-rosters-eight-teams-vic-beasley-martavis-bryant-picks |access-date=2022-12-30 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> The Sea Dragons folded when the XFL and [[USFL (2022)|USFL]] merged to create the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seifert |first=Kevin |date=January 1, 2024 |title=Newly formed United Football League sets 8 markets, tabs coaches |url=https://www.espn.com/xfl/story/_/id/39222541/newly-formed-united-football-league-sets-8-markets-tabs-coaches |access-date=January 15, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

'''Blessuan Austin''' (born July 19, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Rutgers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/college-football/player/_/id/3930021|title=Blessuan Austin Stats, News, Bio|website=[[ESPN.com]]|language=en|url-status=live|accessdate=April 27, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161004093246/http://www.espn.com/college-football/player/_/id/3930021 |archive-date=October 4, 2016 }}</ref>

==Early life==
Austin played the positions of [[cornerback]], [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]], [[quarterback]] and [[wide receiver]] between his years at [[Milford Academy]] and [[Andrew Jackson High School (Queens)|Campus Magnet High School]]. During the 2014 season, Austin recorded 14 tackles and 3 interceptions with the Milford Falcons. His performances earned him All-Queens First Team honors. He was also ranked the No. 8 prospect out of New York by [[Rivals.com]].<ref name="Rutgers B.Austin">[https://scarletknights.com/sports/football/roster/blessuan-austin/5627 "Blessuan Austin"]'s Scarlet Knights Profile. Retrieved October 10, 2024.</ref>

==College career==
Austin began his freshman season at Rutgers University in 2015 as a cornerback with the Scarlet Knights. He started 10 of 11 games in which his season totals included 33 tackles, 4 pass breakups, 1 interception and 1 forced fumble.

During the 2016 season, Austin earned an All-Big Ten honorable mention. In that same season, Austin placed second in the Big Ten and 12th in the national rankings.

In the 2017 season, Austin played in only 4 games before he sustained a left [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] injury against [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska]].<ref name="Rutgers B.Austin"/><ref name="2019 NFL Draft">[https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/nfl/jets/2019/04/27/rutgers-blessuan-austin-jets-sixth-round-nfl-draft-how-cb-fits/3601197002 "North Jersey.com"]'s 2019 NFL Draft Article: Rutgers Blessuan Austin Jets, Sixth-round NFL Draft, How Cb Fits. Retrieved October 10, 2024.</ref> He finished his junior season with a total of 12 tackles, 1 interception and 1 pass breakup.

Austin returned for his senior season in 2018 playing as a [[defensive back]]. His return was short-lived as he sustained another season-ending injury to his left ACL for the second time while against [[Texas State Bobcats football|Texas State]].<ref name="2019 NFL Draft"/> After Austin played his one and only game, his season totals included three tackles, 1 sack and 1 interception. While at Rugers, Austin majored in [[Labour law|labor and employment relations]].<ref name="Rutgers B.Austin"/>

Despite his shortened junior and senior seasons being caused by two consecutive knee injuries, Austin declined to remain at Rutgers as a medical [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] and declared for the 2019 NFL Draft.<ref name="2019 NFL Draft"/>

'''Bo Chapman Nix''' (born February{{nbsp}}25, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]] for the [[Denver Broncos]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played his first three seasons of [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]], winning [[Southeastern Conference football individual awards#Freshman of the Year|SEC Freshman of the Year]] in 2019. During his last two seasons, Nix was a member of the [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon Ducks]] and won [[Pac-12 Conference football individual awards|Pac-12 Offensive Player of the Year]] in 2023 after leading the [[2023 NCAA Division I FBS football season|FBS]] in passing touchdowns and completion percentage.

Nix was selected by Denver in the first round of the [[2024 NFL draft]] and was named the starter as a rookie. He led the Broncos to the playoffs in his first season and to a division title and playoff win in his second, both firsts since 2015.

== Early life ==
Nix was born on February 25, 2000, in [[Arkadelphia, Arkansas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Champlin |first=Drew |date=April 7, 2017 |title=Auburn legacy Bo Nix creating own path as top recruit |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2017/04/son_of_auburn_legacy_elite_pin.html |access-date=March 3, 2024 |website=AL.com}}</ref> He played under his father [[Patrick Nix|Patrick]] at [[Pinson Valley High School]] in [[Pinson, Alabama]], where he accumulated over 12,000 total offensive yards and 161 [[touchdown]]s. Previously, Nix played at [[Scottsboro High School]] in [[Scottsboro, Alabama]], where he passed for 3,463 yards and threw 40 touchdown passes.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://auburntigers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=12878|title=Bo Nix – Football|work=Auburn University Athletics|access-date=July 17, 2019}}</ref> Nix won Alabama's [[Mr. Football Award (Alabama)|Mr. Football Award]] as a senior in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seale |first=Michael |date=January 16, 2019 |title=Bo Nix Named Alabama's Mr. Football For 2018 |url=https://patch.com/alabama/trussville/bo-nix-named-alabamas-mr-football-2018 |access-date=November 12, 2019 |website=Trussville, AL Patch}}</ref> He was rated the top [[dual-threat quarterback]] of his class and committed to play [[college football]] at [[Auburn University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Daniels |first=Tim |date=January 10, 2018 |title=Son of Patrick Nix, 2019 4-Star QB Bo Nix Commits to Auburn |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2753463-son-of-patrick-nix-2019-4-star-qb-bo-nix-commits-to-auburn |access-date=May 19, 2024 |work=Bleacher Report}}</ref>

==College career==
===Auburn===
{{See also|Auburn Tigers football statistical leaders#Passing|label 1 = Auburn Tigers statistical leaders}}
[[File:Bo Nix 2019.png|left|thumb|Nix in 2019]]
As a true freshman at Auburn, Nix was named the starting quarterback for the [[2019 Auburn Tigers football team|2019 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Green |first=Tom |date=August 20, 2019 |title=Freshman Bo Nix named Auburn's starting quarterback |url=https://www.al.com/auburnfootball/2019/08/freshman-bo-nix-named-auburns-starting-quarterback.html |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=AL.com}}</ref> He led Auburn to a 27–21 come-back win against the [[2019 Oregon Ducks football team|Oregon Ducks]] at [[AT&T Stadium]] in [[Arlington, Texas]], on August 31, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2019 |title=Fresh win: Nix rallies No. 16 Auburn 27–21 over No. 11 Ducks |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap?gameId=401110722 |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Nix led Auburn to a 9–4 record in his freshman season, winning the [[Iron Bowl]], 48–45 over Alabama.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zucker |first=Joseph |date=November 30, 2019 |title=Bo Nix, No. 15 Auburn Hang on to Upset No. 5 Alabama in Dramatic 2019 Iron Bowl |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2864896-bo-nix-no-15-auburn-hang-on-to-upset-no-5-alabama-in-dramatic-2019-iron-bowl |access-date=April 10, 2020 |work=Bleacher Report}}</ref> He was voted the [[Southeastern Conference football individual awards|SEC's 2019 Freshman of the Year]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 11, 2019 |title=2019 SEC Football Awards announced |url=https://www.secsports.com/article/28268197/2019-sec-football-awards-announced |access-date=April 10, 2020 |website=SEC Sports}}</ref> finishing the campaign with 16 touchdowns and six interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bo Nix 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bo-nix-1/gamelog/2019 |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref>

Nix threw for 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions as a sophomore in 11 games in the [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on gridiron football#College football|pandemic-shortened]] season in [[2020 Auburn Tigers football team|2020]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 30, 2020 |title=SEC establishes new conference-only football start date |url=https://www.secsports.com/article/29565989/sec-establishes-new-conference-only-football-start-date |access-date=April 10, 2023 |work=SEC Sports |archive-date=March 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230307114416/https://www.secsports.com/article/29565989/sec-establishes-new-conference-only-football-start-date |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bo Nix 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bo-nix-1/gamelog/2020 |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref>

The year [[2021 Auburn Tigers football team|2021]] brought an up-and-down season for Nix, with highlights being leading Auburn to their first win at [[LSU Tigers football|LSU]] since 1999 and a win over #10 [[2021 Ole Miss Rebels football team|Ole Miss]], while also struggling in certain games and being benched for [[T. J. Finley]] in the fourth quarter of a game against [[2021 Georgia State Panthers football team|Georgia State]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 3, 2021 |title=Nix Leads No. 22 Auburn to First Win at LSU Since 1999, 24-19 |url=https://www.waka.com/2021/10/03/nix-leads-no-22-auburn-to-first-win-at-lsu-since-1999-24-19/ |access-date=May 19, 2024 |work=WAKA 8}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 31, 2021 |title=Big Night for Bo Nix as No. 18 Auburn Defeats No. 10 Ole Miss |url=https://www.waka.com/2021/10/30/big-night-for-bo-nix-as-no-18-auburn-defeats-no-10-ole-miss/ |access-date=May 19, 2024 |work=WAKA 8}}</ref> Nix suffered a season-ending injury against [[2021 Mississippi State Bulldogs football team|Mississippi State]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Durando |first=Bennett |date=November 14, 2021 |title=Bo Nix out with broken ankle suffered in Auburn football's loss to Mississippi State |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/auburn/2021/11/14/bo-nix-ankle-injury-auburn-football/8619459002/ |access-date=May 19, 2024 |work=Montgomery Advertiser}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Green |first=Tom |date=September 26, 2021 |title=T.J. Finley replaces Bo Nix, delivers off bench for Auburn in comeback |url=https://www.al.com/auburnfootball/2021/09/tj-finley-replaces-bo-nix-delivers-off-bench-for-auburn-in-comeback.html |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=AL.com}}</ref> He threw for 11 touchdowns and three interceptions in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bo Nix 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bo-nix-1/gamelog/2021 |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> On December 12, 2021, Nix announced he was entering the transfer portal, describing himself as "miserable" while playing under Auburn head coach [[Bryan Harsin]], who had been hired in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hughes |first=Andrew |date=October 28, 2022 |title=Auburn football: Bo Nix says he was 'miserable' every week under Bryan Harsin |url=https://flywareagle.com/2022/10/28/auburn-football-bo-nix-miserable-harsin/ |access-date=August 21, 2023 |work=Fly War Eagle}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Julian |first=Andrew |date=December 13, 2021 |title=Auburn QB Bo Nix enters transfer portal: Three-year starter moves on as graduate student |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/auburn-qb-bo-nix-enters-transfer-portal-three-year-starter-moves-on-as-graduate-student/ |access-date=September 23, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref>

===Oregon===
{{See also|Oregon Ducks football statistical leaders#Passing|label 1=Oregon Ducks statistical leaders}}
[[File:Bo Nix (8120631) (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Nix in 2023]]
In 2022, Nix transferred to the [[University of Oregon]] with two seasons of eligibility remaining based on the NCAA's COVID-19 eligibility waiver for the 2020 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cohen |first=Matt |date=March 1, 2024 |title=Bo Nix says transfer from Auburn to Oregon gave him more freedom |url=https://www.al.com/auburnfootball/2024/03/bo-nix-says-transfer-from-auburn-to-oregon-gave-him-more-freedom.html |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=AL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Durando |first=Bennett |date=December 12, 2021 |title=Auburn football quarterback Bo Nix enters transfer portal |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaaf/2021/12/12/auburn-football-quarterback-bo-nix-enters-transfer-portal/6490495001/ |access-date=December 23, 2021 |work=USA TODAY}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Kercheval|first=Ben|title=Bo Nix transfers to Oregon: Three-year starter for Auburn to finish college career with Ducks|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/bo-nix-transfers-to-oregon-three-year-starter-for-auburn-to-finish-college-career-with-ducks/|url-status=live|access-date=December 23, 2021|website=CBSSports.com|date=December 20, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211220000217/https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/bo-nix-transfers-to-oregon-three-year-starter-for-auburn-to-finish-college-career-with-ducks/ |archive-date=December 20, 2021}}</ref> Nix led Oregon to a 10–3 record in the [[2022 Oregon Ducks football team|2022 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Oregon Ducks Schedule and Results |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/oregon/2022-schedule.html |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> The season saw ranked victories over BYU, UCLA, and Utah before culminating in a narrow 28–27 victory over North Carolina in the Holiday Bowl.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Holiday Bowl - Oregon vs North Carolina Box Score, December 28, 2022 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2022-12-28-north-carolina.html |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Nix finished the season with 3,593 passing yards, 29 touchdowns, and seven interceptions to go along with 89 carries for 510 yards and 14 touchdowns. He also had a receiving touchdown on the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bo Nix 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bo-nix-1/gamelog/2022 |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref>

In the [[2023 Oregon Ducks football team|2023 season]], Nix led Oregon to a successful season, while primarily being in contention for the College Football Playoff. He helped lead the team to a 5–0 start before their first setback against #7 Washington. The team reeled off six consecutive wins to set up a rematch with #3 Washington in the Pac-12 Championship Game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 Oregon Ducks Schedule and Results |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/oregon/2023-schedule.html |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> The Ducks fell to the Huskies once again to fall out of contention for the College Football Playoff.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oregon at Washington Box Score, October 14, 2023 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2023-10-14-washington.html |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Nix passed for 4,508 yards, 45 touchdowns, and three interceptions to go with six rushing touchdowns on the year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bo Nix 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bo-nix-1/gamelog/2023 |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Nix finished third place in the [[Heisman Trophy]] vote behind [[Jayden Daniels]] and [[Michael Penix Jr.]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 Heisman Trophy Voting |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/awards/heisman-2023.html |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Following his final collegiate game in the [[2024 Fiesta Bowl (January)|Fiesta Bowl]] against Liberty, Nix broke [[Mac Jones]]'s previous record for the highest single season completion percentage at 77.45%.<ref name="ncaa23">{{Cite web |title=2023 College Football Leaders |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/years/2023-leaders.html |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Nix led the NCAA in pass completions, completion percentage, and passing touchdowns in 2023.<ref name="ncaa23" /> He started 61 games between Auburn and Oregon, the most in NCAA history for a quarterback.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vinton |first=Jeff |date=January 1, 2024 |title=How Oregon's Bo Nix became a record-setting college football quarterback |url=https://www.12news.com/article/sports/ncaa/ncaaf/bo-nix-oregon-quarterback-record/75-4d39b4ce-fb11-4a1c-a798-81f76f36ff98 |access-date=January 26, 2024 |website=12news.com}}</ref>

=== 2024 season ===
{{See also|2024 Denver Broncos season}}
Nix was selected by the [[Denver Broncos]] in the first round (12th overall) of the [[2024 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos select QB Bo Nix with 12th-overall pick in 2024 NFL Draft|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-select-qb-bo-nix-with-12th-overall-pick-in-2024-nfl-draft|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=April 25, 2024}}</ref> He initially drew the interest of head coach [[Sean Payton]] due to his high completion rate and low negative play differential in college, in addition to an impressive performance in private workouts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Breer |first=Albert |date=August 4, 2025 |title=NFL Takeaways: Bo Nix Is Better Than You Think |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/nfl-takeaways-bo-nix-broncos-chip-kelly-micah-parsons |access-date=August 5, 2025 |website=SI |language=}}</ref> Nix was the last of six quarterbacks taken in the first round, tied with the [[1983 NFL draft|1983 draft]] for the most in NFL history.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Alper |first1=Josh |title=Six quarterbacks in first round ties NFL record |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/six-quarterbacks-in-first-round-ties-nfl-record |website=Pro Football Talk |access-date=April 30, 2024 |date=April 25, 2024}}</ref> On May 11, 2024, he signed his four-year rookie contract, worth $18.6 million fully guaranteed.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 11, 2024 |title=Broncos first-round QB Bo Nix signs rookie contract |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/broncos-first-round-qb-bo-nix-signs-rookie-contract-2024-05-11/ |access-date=June 19, 2024 |website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

On August 22, Nix was named the Broncos' starting quarterback for the season opener against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], becoming the first Broncos rookie to start since [[John Elway]] in 1983.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morse |first=Ben |date=August 22, 2024 |title=Denver Broncos name Bo Nix as 2024 starter, first rookie QB to begin season as team's leader since John Elway |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/08/22/sport/bo-nix-starter-denver-broncos-spt-intl/index.html |access-date=August 28, 2024 |website=CNN.com}}</ref> In his NFL debut against Seattle, Nix completed 26 of 42 passes for 138 yards, two interceptions, and a rushing touchdown during a 26–20 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Booth |first=Tim |date=September 8, 2024 |title=Kenneth Walker III sparks Seahawks rally as Seattle tops Denver 26-20 in Mike Macdonald's debut |url=https://apnews.com/article/broncos-seahawks-score-401254e6f0f616deb77a42bc2f29a445 |access-date=September 9, 2024 |website=AP News}}</ref> His 138 passing yards set an NFL record for the fewest by a quarterback with 25 or more completions in a game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farabaugh |first=Nick |date=September 9, 2024 |title=Next Pittsburgh Steelers opponent sets historically-bad NFL record in debut |url=https://www.pennlive.com/steelers/2024/09/next-pittsburgh-steelers-opponent-sets-historically-bad-nfl-record-in-poor-debut.html |access-date=September 9, 2024 |website=PennLive.com}}</ref> Nix earned his first win in week 3 against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], throwing for 216 yards, a rushing touchdown, and no interceptions in a 26–7 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lowenstein |first=Jack |date=September 22, 2024 |title=Bo Nix records first career victory with Denver Broncos, helps defeat Tampa Bay Buccaneers - CBS Colorado |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/colorado/news/bo-nix-denver-broncos-tampa-bay-buccaneers-nfl-football/ |access-date=October 1, 2024 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref> In week 4, he recorded his first career passing touchdown and led the Broncos to a 10–9 upset victory over the [[New York Jets]] despite ending the first half with negative passing yards and finishing the game with only 60 total passing yards. Additionally, Nix did not allow a turnover or sack for the second consecutive game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Waszak Jr. |first=Dennis |date=September 29, 2024 |title=Nix throws his first NFL touchdown pass to help Broncos slip past Rodgers and the Jets 10-9 |url=https://apnews.com/article/broncos-jets-score-b665c36dbdbede16c2865724139df3e1 |access-date=October 1, 2024 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref>

Nix had a standout October, beginning with a three-touchdown performance in a week 5 victory against the [[Las Vegas Raiders]], followed by 216 passing yards and two touchdowns in week 6 against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McFadden |first=Ryan |date=October 13, 2024 |title=Bo Nix Watch: Rookie QB rebounds after rough first half in loss to Chargers |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2024/10/13/bo-nix-watch-nfl-week-6-broncos-loss-chargers/ |access-date=October 14, 2024 |website=The Denver Post |language=en-US}}</ref> In week 7, he led the Broncos to a dominant 33–10 win over the [[New Orleans Saints]], tying the franchise record for rookie quarterback wins.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Osborn |first=Ally |date=October 18, 2024 |title=Denver Broncos' Bo Nix Ties John Elway, Drew Lock For Rookie Win Record: 'I'm Not Finished' |url=https://www.si.com/college/oregon/football/denver-broncos-bo-nix-ties-john-elway-drew-lock-rookie-quarterback-win-record-oregon-ducks-new-orleans-saints-sean-payton |access-date=October 28, 2024 |website=SI.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He capped the month with 284 passing yards, four total touchdowns, and a 75.7% completion rate in week 8 against the [[Carolina Panthers]], setting a new franchise record with five wins as a rookie. His performances throughout October earned him NFL Offensive Rookie of the Month honors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=October 31, 2024 |title=QB Bo Nix named NFL Offensive Rookie of the Month for October |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/qb-bo-nix-named-nfl-offensive-rookie-of-the-month-for-october |access-date=October 31, 2024 |website=Denver Broncos |language=}}</ref>

In Week 9 against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], Nix caught his first career receiving touchdown on a trick play from receiver [[Courtland Sutton]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pappas |first=Cory |date=November 3, 2024 |title=Denver Broncos' Bo Nix Catches First NFL Touchdown vs. Baltimore Ravens on Trick Play |url=https://www.si.com/college/oregon/football/denver-broncos-bo-nix-catches-first-nfl-touchdown-baltimore-ravens-trick-play-oregon-ducks |access-date=November 14, 2024 |website=Oregon Ducks On SI |language=}}</ref> Nix was named NFL Rookie of the Week in week 10 after throwing for 215 yards, two touchdowns, and orchestrating a late drive that ended with a potential game-winning field goal being blocked in a 16–14 loss to the two-time defending [[Super Bowl]] champion [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kendell |first=Nick |date=November 14, 2024 |title=Broncos QB Bo Nix Named NFL Rookie of the Week |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/broncos/news/broncos-bo-nix-named-nfl-rookie-of-the-week |access-date=November 14, 2024 |website=Denver Broncos On SI |language=}}</ref> The following week against the [[Atlanta Falcons]], Nix went 28-of-33 for a career-high 307 yards and four touchdowns as the Broncos won 38–6. He became the first rookie quarterback in NFL history to complete over 80% of his passes while throwing for at least four touchdowns and 300 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Koplowitz-Fleming |first=Daniel |date=November 18, 2024 |title=NFL stats and records, Week 11: Bo Nix continues his ascent; Jared Goff is perfect again in another win |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/nfl-stats-and-records-week-11-bo-nix-continues-his-ascent-jared-goff-is-perfect-again-in-another-win |access-date=November 19, 2024 |website=NFL.com |language=}}</ref> Following the game, he was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week and Rookie of the Week.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=November 20, 2024 |title=QB Bo Nix named AFC Offensive Player of the Week following win over Falcons |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/qb-bo-nix-named-afc-offensive-player-of-the-week-following-win-over-falcons |access-date=November 20, 2024 |website=Denver Broncos |language=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Weir |first=Susanna |date=November 21, 2024 |title=Bo Nix earns NFL Rookie of the Week award for Week 11 performance vs. Falcons |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/bo-nix-earns-nfl-rookie-of-the-week-award-for-week-11-performance-vs-falcons |access-date=November 21, 2024 |website=Denver Broncos |language=}}</ref> Nix led the Broncos to victories in their next three games to reach 9–5, but losses to the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] and [[Cincinnati Bengals]] put their playoff hopes in jeopardy.<ref>{{Cite news |date=December 15, 2024 |title=Broncos roar back on the strength of 5 takeaways to beat Colts 31-13 and close in on playoff berth |url=https://www.foxsports.com/articles/nfl/broncos-roar-back-on-the-strength-of-5-takeaways-to-beat-colts-3113-and-close-in-on-playoff-berth |access-date=January 5, 2025 |work=Fox Sports|agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Patterson |first=Luke |title=3 Gut-Wrenching Takeaways from Broncos' 30-24 OT Loss to Bengals |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/broncos/news/broncos-lose-bengals-gut-wrenching-takeaways-sean-payton |access-date=January 5, 2025 |work=Sports Illustrated |date=December 28, 2024}}</ref> Needing a win in the final game of the regular season, Nix went 26-of-29 with a then career high 321 yards and four touchdowns in a 38–0 victory over the Chiefs to clinch the Broncos' first playoff berth since [[2015 Denver Broncos season|2015]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Schwab |first=Frank |title=Party like it's 2015: Broncos beat Chiefs to break playoff drought, eliminate Bengals and Dolphins |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/party-like-its-2015-broncos-beat-chiefs-to-break-playoff-drought-eliminate-bengals-and-dolphins-000439676.html |access-date=January 5, 2025 |work=Yahoo Sports |date=January 5, 2025}}</ref> Nix finished the regular season with 29 total passing touchdowns, the second-most ever by a rookie quarterback.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Heath |first=Jon |date=January 24, 2025 |title=Broncos QB Bo Nix had one of the best rookie seasons in NFL history |url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/broncos/2025/01/24/boncos-news-bo-nix-one-of-the-best-rookie-seasons-nfl-history/77925234007/ |access-date=August 5, 2025 |website=Broncos Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

In the [[2024–25 NFL playoffs#AFC: Buffalo Bills 31, Denver Broncos 7|Wild Card round]], Nix was held in check, finishing 13-for-22 with 144 yards passing and one touchdown with 43 rushing yards as the Broncos fell 7–31 to the [[2024 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Broncos rookie QB Bo Nix learns difficult, but valuable lesson in losing playoff debut against Bills |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/broncos-rookie-qb-bo-nix-011232891.html |access-date=January 13, 2025 |agency=Associated Press |publisher=Yahoo Sports |date=January 12, 2025}}</ref> Nix's sole touchdown, a 43-yard pass to [[Troy Franklin]], was the first rookie-to-rookie touchdown pass in NFL playoff history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Douglas |first=Stephen |date=January 12, 2025 |title=Bo Nix, Troy Franklin Made Wild NFL Playoff History on Broncos' Long TD vs. Bills |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bo-nix-troy-franklin-made-wild-nfl-playoff-history-on-broncos-long-td-vs-bills |access-date=January 20, 2025 |website=SI |language=}}</ref> Following the Broncos' elimination, Nix revealed that he had played with [[transverse process]] fractures in his back since Week 12.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 13, 2025 |title=Broncos' Bo Nix says he played through back fractures this season |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/43401734/broncos-qb-bo-nix-says-played-back-fractures |access-date=January 24, 2025 |website=espn.com |language=en}}</ref>

Nix was originally the fourth alternate AFC Quarterback in the [[2025 Pro Bowl Games|Pro Bowl]], but was invited to play due to opt-outs. However, due to a previously scheduled minor postseason cleanup procedure, he also had to decline.<ref name="k625">{{cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=January 28, 2025 |title=Report: C.J. Stroud declined Pro Bowl nod; injury kept Bo Nix from participating |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/report-c-j-stroud-declined-pro-bowl-nod-bo-nixs-injury-kept-him-out |access-date=January 31, 2025 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref>

Nix was a finalist for [[Offensive Rookie of the Year|NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year]], placing third behind [[Jayden Daniels]] and [[Brock Bowers]].<ref>{{cite web | title=NFL Honors: Finalists announced for MVP, other awards from 2024 season | website=NFL.com | date=January 23, 2025 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/nfl-honors-finalists-announced-for-mvp-other-awards-from-2024-season | access-date=January 20, 2026}}</ref> He was voted the 64th-best player in the league in the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2025|Top 100 Players of 2025]] by his NFL peers following his successful rookie campaign.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rehklau |first=Kennedy |date=July 24, 2025 |title=QB Bo Nix voted No. 64 on 2025 NFL Top 100 list |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/qb-bo-nix-voted-no-64-on-2025-nfl-top-100-list |access-date=July 24, 2025 |website=Denver Broncos |language=}}</ref>

=== 2025 season ===
{{See also|2025 Denver Broncos season}}
[[File:Bo Nix Salute to Service 2025 (cropped).webp|thumb|Nix in 2025]]
On July 23, 2025, Broncos head coach [[Sean Payton]] revealed that Nix spent a portion of the offseason working with former Saints quarterback [[Drew Brees]] and throwing mechanics specialist [[Tom House]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Legwold |first=Jeff |date=July 23, 2025 |title=Broncos' Nix met with Brees, 'wants to improve' |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/45806437/broncos-nix-met-brees-wants-improve-says-payton |access-date=July 24, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |language=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Melendrez Stapleton |first=Arnie |date=July 23, 2025 |title=Sean Payton says Bo Nix huddled with Drew Brees, Tom House this offseason as he prepares for Year 2 |url=https://apnews.com/article/denver-broncos-bo-nix-sean-payton-336d889d52c4323e100308a22e79b40a |access-date=July 24, 2025 |website=AP News |language=}}</ref>

During Week 7 against the [[2025 New York Giants season|New York Giants]], Nix became the first player in NFL history to have at least two passing and two rushing touchdowns in a single quarter in a comeback victory after being down 19–0 to begin the fourth quarter. The Broncos scored a total of 33 points to win 33–32, the most in a game by any team held scoreless through three quarters in league history and the second most points scored in the fourth quarter in NFL history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Legwold |first=Jeff |last2=Raanan |first2=Jordan |date=October 20, 2025 |title=How did the Broncos go from down 19-0 to beat the Giants? Breaking down a wild fourth quarter |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46654605/broncos-fourth-quarter-comeback-win-33-points-giants-interception-loss |access-date=October 20, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |language=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Breech |first=John |date=October 19, 2025 |title=Broncos set two NFL records in stunning comeback win over Giants: How Denver rewrote the record book |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/broncos-set-two-nfl-records-in-stunning-comeback-win-over-giants-how-denver-rewrote-the-record-book/ |access-date=October 20, 2025 |website=CBS Sports |language=}}</ref>

Nix had a career game in Week 15, going 23 of 34 for 302 yards and four touchdowns and a passer rating of 134.7 in a playoff-clinching 34–26 victory against the [[2025 Green Bay Packers season| 
Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keeler |first=Sean |date=December 15, 2025 |title=Broncos four downs: Bo Nix's best NFL game carries Denver to 11th straight win |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2025/12/14/broncos-packers-bo-nix-week-15/ |access-date=December 15, 2025 |website=The Denver Post |language=}}</ref> For his performance, Nix was named a [[FedEx Air & Ground NFL Players of the Week|FedEx Air & Ground Player of the Week]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=December 17, 2025 |title=Broncos QB Bo Nix named FedEx Air & Ground Player of the Week following win over Packers |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-qb-bo-nix-named-fedex-air-and-ground-player-of-the-week-following-win-over-packers |access-date=December 17, 2025 |website=Denver Broncos |language=}}</ref>

In Week 18, the Broncos defeated the [[2025 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]] 19–3, securing them the top seed in the AFC. Despite a relatively pedestrian stat line of 14 for 23 and 141 yards, Nix set the record for the most wins ever in a single regular season by a Broncos quarterback with 14 while simultaneously tying [[Russell Wilson]] for the NFL record of the most regular season wins by a quarterback through two seasons with 24.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Inabinett|first=Mark|date=January 4, 2026|title=Broncos get AFC No. 1 seed, Bo Nix gets piece of NFL record |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2026/01/broncos-get-afc-no-1-seed-bo-nix-gets-piece-of-nfl-record.html |access-date=January 5, 2026 |website=al.com |language=en}}</ref>

After the first round bye, Nix and the Broncos were set to play the [[2025 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]] in the [[2025–26_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Denver_Broncos_33,_Buffalo_Bills_30_(OT)|Divisional Round]] in a playoff rematch from last year. Nix completed 26 of 46 attempts for 279 yards, and threw for three touchdowns with one interception as the Broncos won in overtime 33–30, marking their first playoff win since [[Super Bowl 50]] at the end of the [[2015 Denver Broncos season|2015 season]]. With this win, Nix holds the record for the most game winning drives in a season by a quarterback age 25 or younger (8).<ref>https://www.instagram.com/p/DTok2IljP7B/</ref> However, during the third-to-last play of the game, Nix suffered a broken ankle, ending his season.<ref>{{cite web | last=Walker | first=Brandon | title=Denver Broncos: Sean Payton details Bo Nix's injury reaction | website=Broncos Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=January 18, 2026 | url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/broncos/2026/01/18/broncos-sean-payton-details-bo-nixs-injury-reaction/88245654007/ | access-date=January 26, 2026}}</ref> He was officially placed on [[Injured reserve list|injured reserve]] on January 24, 2026.<ref>{{cite web | last=DiLalla | first=Aric | title=Broncos activate C Luke Wattenberg from IR, place QB Bo Nix on IR | website=Denver Broncos | date=January 24, 2026 | url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-activate-c-luke-wattenberg-from-ir-place-qb-bo-nix-on-ir | access-date=January 26, 2026}}</ref>

'''Blake Whittfield Ferguson''' (born April 21, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[long snapper]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]], winning a national championship in 2020.

==Early life==
Ferguson attended [[Buford High School (Georgia)]] in [[Buford, Georgia]] where he was ranked as the number one long snapper nationally by Scout and 247Sports. He was rated as two-star prospect by Rivals, ESPN, 247Sports and Scout. He earned an invitation to play in the Army All-American game. During his high school career, he helped lead his team to three state titles in his prep career. He was the recipient of the Chris Rubio Award which is given to the nation's top high school long snapper as a junior and senior.<ref>{{cite web |title=Blake Ferguson |url=https://lsusports.net/sports/fb/roster/player/blake-ferguson/ |website=LSU |access-date=7 June 2024 |date=8 July 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
Ferguson played [[college football]] for [[LSU Tigers football|LSU]] from 2015 to 2019. He played in 52 games at [[long snapper]], and was also a two-year [[captain (sports)|captain]] of the team.<ref name="WAFB">{{cite web |last1=Auzenne |first1=Josh |title=2020 NFL DRAFT: LSU LS Blake Ferguson chosen in 6th round (No. 185 overall) by Miami Dolphins |url=https://www.fox8live.com/2020/04/25/nfl-draft-lsu-ls-blake-ferguson-chosen-th-round-no-overall-by-miami-dolphins/ |website=WAFB |access-date=April 28, 2020 |date=April 25, 2020}}</ref>

On August 20, 2025, Ferguson signed with the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Houston Texans Transactions (8-20-2025) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-8-20-2025 |website=houstontexans.com |access-date=21 August 2025}}</ref> He was released on August 26 as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Houston Texans Transactions (08-26-2025) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-08-26-2025 |website=houstontexans.com |access-date=27 August 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ferguson's parents are Tracy and Kevin Ferguson. He is the younger brother of [[Buffalo Bills]] long snapper [[Reid Ferguson]]. He has [[type 1 diabetes]].<ref name="buffalobills.com">{{cite web |last1=Brown |first1=Chris |title=Brotherly bond: Blake Ferguson aims to join his mentor and brother Reid Ferguson in the NFL |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/brotherly-bond-blake-ferguson-aims-to-join-his-mentor-and-brother-reid-ferguson- |website=Buffalo Bills |access-date=April 28, 2020 |date=January 25, 2020}}</ref>

In July 2024, Ferguson married Abbey Hale.{{cn|date=November 2024}}

Ferguson has been an outspoken conservative on social media, supporting the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] as well as candidates like [[Donald Trump]] and [[Ron DeSantis]]. He holds [[Anti-abortion movements|pro-life views on abortion]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Schad |first1=Joe |title=Some folks ask Dolphins' Blake Ferguson to shut up and snap. 'I'm going to get my point across.' |url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/nfl/dolphins/2024/08/30/miami-dolphins-snapper-blake-ferguson-conservative-views/74918807007/ |website=[[The Palm Beach Post]] |access-date=31 December 2024}}</ref>

'''Thakarius''' "'''BoPete'''" '''Keyes''' (born November 9, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Tulane Green Wave football|Tulane]], and was selected by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in the seventh round of the [[2020 NFL draft]]. He has also been a member of the [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[New England Patriots]], [[Chicago Bears]], [[Houston Texans]], [[Atlanta Falcons]], [[Baltimore Ravens]], and [[Cleveland Browns]].

==College career==
According to WGNO, in 2019, Keyes started every game for Tulane and held opposing [[quarterbacks]] to a 45 percent completion rate when he was targeted. He earned an Honorable Mention for the [[American Athletic Conference]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 25, 2020 |title=Tulane DB Thakarius Keyes Selected by Kansas City in 2020 NFL Draft |url=https://wgno.com/sports/tulane-db-thakarius-keyes-selected-by-kansas-city-in-2020-nfl-draft/ |access-date=April 25, 2020 |website=WGNO}}</ref> In his junior and senior seasons, Keyes had 85 tackles, 18 passes defended and two [[interceptions]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldman |first=Charles |date=April 25, 2020 |title=Chiefs trade up into seventh round, select Tulane CB Thakarius 'Bopete' Keyes |url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2020/04/25/kansas-city-chiefs-trade-up-into-seventh-round-select-tulane-cb-thakarius-keyes/ |access-date=April 25, 2020 |website=Chiefs Wire}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Kansas City Chiefs===
Keyes was selected by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] in the seventh round of the [[2020 NFL draft]] with the 237th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 25, 2020 |title=Chiefs' Thakarius Keyes: Grabbed by Chiefs |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/chiefs-thakarius-keyes-grabbed-by-chiefs/ |access-date=April 25, 2020 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> He was placed on the active/[[non-football injury list]] on July 26.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldman |first=Charles |date=July 26, 2020 |title=Chiefs rookie CB BoPete Keyes placed on non-football injury list |url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2020/07/26/kansas-city-chiefs-bopete-keyes-non-football-injury-list/ |access-date=July 27, 2020 |website=USAToday.com}}</ref> Keyes was activated on August 16.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 16, 2020 |title=Chiefs Thakarius Keyes back at practice |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/chiefs-thakarius-keyes-back-at-practice/ |access-date=August 17, 2020 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> He finished his rookie season playing in eight games and recording eight total tackles. On August 31, 2021, Keyes was waived by the Chiefs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 31, 2021 |title=Chiefs Announce Roster Moves to Meet NFL-Mandated 53 Players |url=https://www.chiefs.com/news/chiefs-announce-roster-moves-to-meet-nfl-mandated-53-players |access-date=2023-07-17 |website=Chiefs.com}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On September 1, 2021, Keyes was claimed off waivers by the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Claim Cornerbacks Thakarius Keyes, Chris Wilcox Off Waivers; Waive Marvell Tell III, Andre Chachere|url=https://www.colts.com/news/waiver-claim-thakarius-bopete-keyes-chris-wilcox-marvell-tell-andre-chachere|website=Colts.com|date=September 1, 2021}}</ref> He was waived on November 13 and re-signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Activate CB T.J. Carrie From Injured Reserve, Waive CB BoPete Keyes, Elevate S Jahleel Addae To Active Roster From Practice Squad|url=https://www.colts.com/news/tj-carrie-injured-reserve-activated-bopete-keyes-jahleel-addae|website=Colts.com|date=November 13, 2021}}</ref> Keyes was released by the Colts on November 22.<ref>{{cite web|title= Colts Sign Anthony Chesley, Brian Poole To Practice Squad, Release BoPete Keyes From Practice Squad|url= https://www.colts.com/news/anthony-chesley-brian-poole-signed-practice-squad-bopete-keys-released|website=Colts.com|date=November 22, 2021}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On November 30, 2021, Keyes was signed to the [[New England Patriots]]' practice squad, but was released the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots Sign DB Thakarius (BoPete) Keyes and RB Devine Ozigbo to the Practice Squad; Release DL Niles Scott|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-db-thakarius-bopete-keyes-and-rb-devine-ozigbo-to-the-practice-squ|website=Patriots.com|date=November 30, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots release kicker Quinn Nordin; Release DB Thakarius (BoPete) Keyes from the practice squad|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-release-kicker-quinn-nordin-release-db-thakarius-bopete-keyes-from-the-|website=Patriots.com|date=December 1, 2021}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On December 15, 2021, Keyes was signed to the [[Chicago Bears]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=December 15, 2021 |title=Roster Move: Bears put Borom on COVID-19 list |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-move-bears-put-borom-on-covid-19-list |access-date=2022-06-24 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Bears on January 11, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=January 11, 2022 |title=Roster Moves: Bears sign 11 to reserve/future contracts |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-sign-11-to-reserve-future-contracts |access-date=2022-06-24 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref> Keyes was waived on August 23.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=August 23, 2022 |title=Roster Moves: Bears cut five to reach 80-man roster limit |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-cut-five-to-reach-80-man-roster-limit |access-date=2024-07-08 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref>

===Houston Texans (first stint)===
On September 13, 2022, Keyes was signed to the [[Houston Texans]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lane |first=Mark |date=September 13, 2022 |title=Texans sign former Chiefs cornerback BoPete Keyes to practice squad |url=https://texanswire.usatoday.com/2022/09/13/texans-sign-bopete-keyes-practice-squad/ |access-date=2024-07-08 |website=Texans Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> He was released on October 18.

===Atlanta Falcons===
On October 25, 2022, Keyes was signed to the [[Atlanta Falcons]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McElhaney |first=Tori |date=October 25, 2022 |title=Falcons release former second round NFL Draft pick |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-release-former-second-round-nfl-draft-pick-marlon-davidson |access-date=2024-07-08 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref> He was released on November 8.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bair |first=Scott |date=November 8, 2022 |title=Falcons place offensive lineman on IR, sign safety off practice squad among other roster moves |url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-matt-hennessy-jovante-moffatt-panthers-injured-reserve |access-date=2024-07-08 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com}}</ref>

===Houston Texans (second stint)===
On November 17, 2022, Keyes was signed to the Houston Texans' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 16, 2022 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (11-16-2022) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-11-16-2022 |access-date=2024-07-08 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> He was released later that day.<ref name="g221">{{cite web | last=Lane | first=Mark | title=Texans release CB BoPete Keyes from practice squad | website=Texans Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2022-11-18 | url=https://texanswire.usatoday.com/2022/11/18/texans-release-bopete-keyes/ | access-date=2025-01-08}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On December 7, 2022, Keyes was signed to the [[Baltimore Ravens]]' practice squad. He signed a reserve/future contract with Baltimore on January 16, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mink |first=Ryan |date=January 16, 2023 |title=Ravens Sign Six Players to Reserve/Future Deals |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-sign-six-players-reserve-future-deals |access-date=2024-07-08 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref> On May 12, Keyes was waived by the Ravens.<ref name="d592">{{cite web | title=BoPete Keyes: Waived by Baltimore | website=CBSSports.com | date=2023-05-12 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/bopete-keyes-waived-by-baltimore/ | access-date=2025-01-08}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
On July 6, 2023, Keyes was signed by the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-cb-thakarius-keyes|title=Browns sign CB Thakarius Keyes|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=July 6, 2023|access-date=July 7, 2023}}</ref> He was waived by Cleveland on July 29.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kinnan |first=Cory |date=2023-07-29 |title=Browns open up roster spot, waive CB Bopete Keyes with injury designation |url=https://brownswire.usatoday.com/2023/07/29/browns-waive-bopete-keyes-injury/ |access-date=2024-07-08 |website=Browns Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== San Antonio Brahmas ===
On February 25, 2024, Keyes signed with he [[San Antonio Brahmas]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL).<ref>{{cite news |title=UFL Player Transactions, Sunday February 25, 2024 |url=https://uflboard.com/news/ufl-player-transactions-sunday-february-25-2024/ |website=UFLBoard.com |date=February 25, 2024 |access-date=February 28, 2024}}</ref> He re-signed with the team on August 27.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=UFL_PR |title=The #UFL has announced the following transactions |number=1828545008779297271 |date=August 27, 2024 |access-date=August 27, 2024}}</ref> Keyes was released on May 14, 2025.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Larsen |first1=James |title=Brahmas Sign CB Sean Fresch, Cut BoPete Keyes |url=https://pfnewsroom.com/news/brahmas-sign-cb-sean-fresch-cut-bopete-keyes/ |website=PFnewsroom |access-date=14 May 2025}}</ref>

===Montreal Alouettes===

On January 28, 2026 Keyes signed with the [[Montreal Alouettes]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Transactions - Football Player Trades and Signings |url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/ |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=CFL.ca |language=en}}</ref> He was released on May 31, 2026.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/thakarius-keyes-keyesth01/transactions | title=Thakarius Keyes | publisher=FootballDB.com | accessdate=11 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Blake Thomas Gillikin''' (born January 21, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Punter (gridiron football)|punter]] for the [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]].

Gillikin is second in NFL history in yards per punt ({{#invoke:Math|round|{{#invoke:Math|divide|13132|271}}|2}}).{{efn|Minimum 250 punts. Ranks just behind [[AJ Cole (American football)|AJ Cole]] ({{#invoke:Math|round|{{#invoke:Math|divide|21572|445}}|2}}).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Most yards per punt in NFL history (minimum 250 punts) |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/stathead/football/player-season-finder.cgi |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20260106200313/https://www.sports-reference.com/stathead/tiny/hk130 |archive-date=January 6, 2026 |access-date=January 6, 2026 |website=[[Stathead]]}}</ref>}}

==Early life==
A former resident of [[Smyrna, Georgia]], Gillikin helped lead [[The Westminster Schools]] to its first GHSA Football Class AAA Georgia State Championship since 1978 in 2015, and was rated as a five-star punter and a five-star kicker by Kohl's Kicking Camp.

==College career==
A four-year starter at Penn State, Gillikin is ranked No. 2 on Penn State's career punting average charts (43.03 avg.) He landed 53 career punts downed inside the opponent's ten-yard line (seven in 2016, 18 in 2017, 12 in 2018, 15 in 2019) and is the only player in program history with seven punts of 65 or more yards. Gillikin is second all time in net punting yards in school history behind Jeremy Kapinos. In 2019, Gillikin averaged 42.2 yards per punt as was selected [[List of All-Big Ten Conference football teams|All-Big Ten Conference]] honorable mention by the conference coaches and media. Was also selected for the CoSIDA Academic [[All-American]] first-team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Penn State Football |url=https://gopsusports.com/sports/football/roster/blake-gillikin/9500 |access-date=September 15, 2020 |website=Penn State Nittany Lions Athletics}}</ref>

=== New Orleans Saints ===
Gillikin signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on April 27, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Gillikin |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/team/players-roster/blake-gillikin/ |access-date=September 15, 2020 |website=New Orleans Saints}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on September 9.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=September 9, 2020 |title=Saints place backup punter on injured reserve |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/09/09/saints-place-backup-punter-on-injured-reserve/ |access-date=September 25, 2020 |website=NBCSports.com}}</ref>

Gillikin was named the Saints starting punter for the 2021 season after the team released longtime starter [[Thomas Morstead]] in the offseason.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sigler |first=John |date=August 24, 2021 |title=Blake Gillikin, Thomas Morstead's former understudy, wins Saints punter competition |url=https://saintswire.usatoday.com/2021/08/24/saints-punter-blake-gillikin-nfl-penn-state-news/ |access-date=January 3, 2022|publisher=USA Today |website=Saints Wire |language=en-US}}</ref>

Gillikin did not receive a qualifying offer following the 2022 season and became a free agent on March 15, 2023.<ref name="v278">{{cite web | last=Holt | first=Adam | title=Saints make a surprising decision at the beginning of free agency | website=A to Z Sports | date=2023-03-15 | url=https://atozsports.com/nfl/new-orleans-saints-news/saints-blake-gillikin-decision-free-agency-news-nfl/ | access-date=2025-01-08}}</ref> On March 16, Gillikin re-signed with the Saints.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Camer |first=Jonny |date=March 16, 2023 |title=Saints re-sign P Blake Gillikin competition |url=https://www.canalstreetchronicles.com/2023/3/16/23643811/saints-re-sign-p-blake-gillikin |access-date=March 17, 2023|publisher=SBNation.com |website=Canal Street Chronicles }}</ref> He was waived on August 29, after losing the punting battle to [[Lou Hedley]].<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-roster-53-reductions-2023-nfl-season|website=NewOrleansSaints.com|date=August 29, 2023}}</ref>

=== Arizona Cardinals ===
On October 3, 2023, Gillikin was signed by the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=October 3, 2023 |title=Cardinals Make Roster Change At Punter |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-make-roster-change-at-punter |access-date=October 4, 2023 |website=AZCardinals.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

In Week 9 of the 2024 season, Gillikin punted four times with three inside the 20-yard line in a 29-9 win over the [[2024 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]], earning NFC Special Teams Player of the Week.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets WR Garrett Wilson, Eagles RB Saquon Barkley highlight Players of the Week|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2024-week-9-garrett-wilson-saquon-barkley|author=Gordon, Grant|website=NFL.com|date=November 6, 2024}}</ref>

On October 11, 2025, Gillikin was placed on injured reserve due to a lingering back injury.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cardinals' Blake Gillikin: Lands on IR with back injury|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/cardinals-blake-gillikin-lands-on-ir-with-back-injury/|access-date=November 29, 2025|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref>

On March 8, 2026, Gillikin re-signed with the Cardinals on a one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cardinals re-sign Chad Ryland, Blake Gillikin|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/cardinals-re-sign-chad-ryland-blake-gillikin|access-date=March 9, 2026|website=nbcsports.com|language=en}}</ref>

'''Blake Lynch''' (born February 14, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor Bears]], and has previously played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Minnesota Vikings]] and [[Los Angeles Chargers]].

==College career==
Born in [[Gilmer, Texas]], Lynch attended [[Gilmer Independent School District|Gilmer High School]], where he played alongside future Vikings teammate [[Kris Boyd (American football)|Kris Boyd]]. After [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] in his freshman year, he played [[college football]] for [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor]], where he made 32 career starts at five different positions ([[cornerback]], linebacker, [[safety (gridiron football position)|safety]], [[wide receiver]] and [[running back]]). In a four-year college career, he accrued 673 receiving yards, four receiving touchdowns and 79 rushing yards.<ref>{{cite web |title=Blake Lynch |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/blake-lynch-1.html |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |publisher=Sports Reference |accessdate=December 21, 2020 }}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
Lynch was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] following the [[2020 NFL draft]] on April 28, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Peters |first1=Craig |last2=Smith |first2=Eric |last3=Young |first3=Lindsey |title=A Dozen Join Vikings as 2020 Undrafted Rookie Free Agents |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/a-dozen-join-vikings-as-2020-undrafted-rookie-free-agents |website=Vikings.com |date=April 28, 2020 |access-date=January 27, 2021}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts on September 5,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Peters |first1=Craig |last2=Smith |first2=Eric |title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves, Set Initial 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/2020-roster-53-man-announced |website=Vikings.com |date=September 5, 2020 |access-date=January 27, 2021}}</ref> and signed to the team's [[practice squad]] the following day.<ref>{{cite news |title=Vikings Claim LB Ryan Connelly, Add 13 Players To Practice Squad |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/ryan-connelly-2020-practice-squad-add-13-players |website=Vikings.com |date=September 6, 2020 |access-date=January 27, 2021}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on December 12 for the team's week 14 game against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], and reverted to the practice squad after the game.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=Vikings |title=The #Vikings have signed LB Hardy Nickerson (@younghardy_) to the active roster. LB Blake Lynch has been elevated to the active roster for #MINvsTB and S Curtis Riley has been waived. |number=1337842334570967040 |date=December 12, 2020 |access-date=January 27, 2021}}</ref> He played 13 snaps on special teams, and his only statistical contribution was a downed punt at the end of the Vikings' first drive of the game. He was promoted to the active roster on December 16,<ref>{{cite news |title=Vikings Waive CB Mark Fields II, Sign LB Blake Lynch from Practice Squad to Active Roster |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/mark-fields-blake-lynch-roster-moves |website=Vikings.com |date=December 16, 2020 |access-date=January 27, 2021}}</ref> and played in the game against the [[Chicago Bears]]. He played one defensive snap, contributing one tackle assist, and 16 special teams snaps, making one tackle on kick coverage in the game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Blake Lynch |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LyncBl00.htm |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |publisher=Sports Reference |accessdate=December 21, 2020 }}</ref>

On August 30, 2022, Lynch was waived by the Vikings.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/roster-moves-initial-53-man-waived-injured-2022|title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves, Set Initial 53-Man Roster|website=Vikings.com|date=August 30, 2022}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On October 18, 2022, Lynch was signed to the [[Arizona Cardinals]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cardinals Add Kicker Rodrigo Blankenship To Practice Squad |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-add-kicker-rodrigo-blankenship-to-practice-squad |access-date=2022-10-18 |website=AZCardinals.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 11, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bernhard Seikovits Among 14 'Futures' Cardinals Sign For 2023|url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/bernhard-seikovits-among-14-futures-cardinals-sign-for-2023|author=Urban, Darren|website=AZCardinals.com|date=January 11, 2023}}</ref> Lynch was released by the Cardinals on May 15.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cardinals Sign Veteran Punter Matt Haack |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-sign-veteran-punter-matt-haack |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=AZCardinals.com }}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers (first stint)===
On July 28, 2023, Lynch signed with the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Chargers Sign Blake Lynch |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-sign-blake-lynch |access-date=2023-07-28 |website=Chargers.com }}</ref> He was waived on August 29, and re-signed to the practice squad on October 24.<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers Reduce Roster to 53 Players|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-reduce-roster-to-53-players-2023|website=Chargers.com|date=August 29, 2023}}</ref> Lynch was signed to the active roster on November 21.<ref>{{cite web |title=Los Angeles Chargers Place Tanner Muse on Injured Reserve; Sign Blake Lynch to Active Roster |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-place-tanner-muse-on-injured-reserve-sign-blake-lynch-to-ac |website=chargers.com |access-date=22 November 2023}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
On August 5, 2024, Lynch signed with the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign LB Blake Lynch|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-lb-blake-lynch|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=August 5, 2024}}</ref> He was released on August 27.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Make Roster Moves, Establish Initial 2024 53-Man Roster|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-make-roster-moves-establish-initial-2024-53-man-roster|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers (second stint)===
On September 24, 2024, Lynch signed with the Los Angeles Chargers practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Peterson |first1=Michael |title=Chargers sign LB Blake Lynch, WR Jalen Reagor to practice squad |url=https://www.boltsfromtheblue.com/2024/9/24/24253463/chargers-blake-lynch-jalen-reagor-vikings-eagles-patriots |website=SB Nation |access-date=25 September 2024}}</ref> He was released on October 15.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Borquez |first1=Gavino |title=Chargers sign TE McCallan Castles to practice squad |url=https://chargerswire.usatoday.com/2024/10/15/chargers-roster-practice-squad-mccallan-castles/ |website=Chargers Wire |access-date=16 October 2024}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On October 16, 2024, Lynch signed with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Owen |first1=Carter |title=Raiders sign LB Blake Lynch to practice squad |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-blake-lynch-linebacker-to-practice-squad-nfl-transactions-2024 |website=raiders.com |access-date=17 October 2024}}</ref> He was released on November 19.

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On December 30, 2024, Lynch was signed to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs add linebacker to practice squad|url=https://www.arrowheadpride.com/2024/12/30/24332454/chiefs-add-linebacker-to-practice-squad|work=Arrowhead Pride|date=December 30, 2024}}</ref> He was released on January 7, 2025.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ediger |first1=Jon |title=Chiefs release standout LB, re-sign speedy WR |url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2025/01/07/chiefs-release-blake-lynch-sign-montrell-washington/ |website=Chiefs Wire |access-date=8 January 2025}}</ref> On March 3, Lynch re-signed with the Chiefs.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chiefs re-sign LB Blake Lynch|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/chiefs-re-sign-lb-blake-lynch|access-date=March 5, 2025|website=nbcsports.com|language=en}}</ref> On May 3, Lynch was waived by the Chiefs.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=Charean |title=Chiefs cut DE BJ Thompson, LB Blake Lynch |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/chiefs-cut-de-bj-thompson-lb-blake-lynch |website=NBC Sports |access-date=6 May 2025}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On August 12, 2025, Lynch signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wyatt |first1=Jim |title=Titans Sign LBs Khaleke Hudson and Blake Lynch, while Waiving LB David Gbenda and Waiving/Injured LB Anfernee Orji |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-lbs-khaleke-hudson-and-blake-lynch-while-waiving-lb-david-gbenda-and-waiving-injured-lb-anfernee-orji |website=tennesseetitans.com |access-date=13 August 2025}}</ref> He was released on August 26 as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wyatt |first1=Jim |title=Titans Part Ways With 20 Players Ahead of Today's Deadline, While Placing RB Tyjae Spears on Injured Reserve (Designated for Return) |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-part-ways-with-20-players-ahead-of-today-s-deadline-while-placing-rb-tyjae-spears-on-injured-reserve-designated-for-return |website=tennesseetitans.com |access-date=27 August 2025}}</ref>
