===Buffalo Bills===
After playing four years at [[Northwestern Wildcats football|Northwestern]], Hance was signed by the [[Buffalo Bills]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 9, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Dallas |date=May 9, 2020 |title=Bills Sign Cody Ford, Five Other Draft Picks, Eight UDFAs |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2019/05/bills-sign-cody-ford-five-other-draft-picks-eight-udfas |access-date=January 5, 2021 |website=ProFootballRumors.com}}</ref> However, he was soon released on May 22.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Chris |date=May 9, 2020 |title=Bills awarded waiver claim for T De'Ondre Wesley, sign TE Mik'Quan Deane |url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-awarded-waiver-claim-for-t-de-ondre-wesley-sign-te-mik-quan-deane |access-date=January 5, 2021 |website=BuffaloBills.com}}</ref>

===Washington Football Team===
On June 3, 2019, Hance was signed by the [[Washington Football Team]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Links |first=Zach |date=June 3, 2019 |title=Minor NFL Transactions: 6/3/19 |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2019/06/minor-nfl-transactions-6319 |access-date=January 5, 2021 |website=ProFootballRumors.com}}</ref> where he spent the rest of [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]], being waived on August 31.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ortenberg |first=Andrew |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Redskins Get Down To 53 |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2019/08/redskins-get-down-to-53 |access-date=January 5, 2021 |website=ProFootballRumors.com}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On September 1, 2019, Hance was signed by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] to their [[practice squad]], where he spent the entire 2019 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Werner |first=Barry |date=September 1, 2019 |title=UPDATED: Practice squad signees for all 32 NFL teams |url=https://touchdownwire.usatoday.com/gallery/practice-squad-signees-for-all-32-nfl-teams/ |access-date=January 5, 2021 |website=USAToday.com}}</ref> Afterward, he was signed to a reserve/futures contract on January 2, 2020,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reid |first=John |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Jaguars claim former Cowboys safety Josh Jones off waivers; sign seven players to reserve/future contracts |url=https://www.jacksonville.com/story/sports/nfl/2020/01/02/jaguars-claim-former-cowboys-safety-josh-jones-off-waivers-sign-seven-players-to-reservefuture-contracts/112136560/ |access-date=January 5, 2021 |website=Jacksonville.com}}</ref> but was waived on September 5.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hill |first=Kassidy |date=September 5, 2020 |title=Jaguars Make Final Roster Cuts, Set Initial 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/jaguars/news/jacksonville-jaguars-make-final-roster-cuts-set-53-man-roster |access-date=January 5, 2021 |website=SI.com}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
On September 22, 2020, Hance was signed by the [[New York Jets]] to their practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=September 22, 2020 |title=Jets Sign 3 Players to Practice Squad |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-3-players-to-practice-squad |access-date=January 5, 2021 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
On January 2, 2021, Hance was signed by the [[Cleveland Browns]] from the Jets' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 2, 2021 |title=Browns make roster moves |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-make-roster-moves-x7526 |access-date=January 5, 2021 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref> Because of injuries and players inactive due to positive [[COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19 tests]], he was activated for the Browns' [[2020–21 NFL playoffs#AFC: Cleveland Browns 48, Pittsburgh Steelers 37|playoff game]] against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. He made his NFL debut in the fourth quarter,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mathes |first=Dennis |date=January 10, 2021 |title=Jacksonville grad Blake Hance makes NFL debut as Cleveland drills Steelers 48–37 |url=https://www.myjournalcourier.com/sports/article/Jacksonville-grad-Blake-Hance-makes-NFL-debut-as-15860449.php |access-date=January 11, 2021 |website=MyJournalCourier.com}}</ref> playing 14 snaps.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=January 12, 2021 |title='Guy named Blake' Hance reflects on sudden playing time in Browns' wild-card win: 'It's what you want' |work=NFL.com |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/guy-named-blake-hance-reflects-on-sudden-playing-time-in-browns-wild-card-win-it |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113223939/https://www.nfl.com/news/guy-named-blake-hance-reflects-on-sudden-playing-time-in-browns-wild-card-win-it |archive-date=January 13, 2021}}</ref> Browns quarterback [[Baker Mayfield]] complimented Hance while noting they had not had a chance to practice together. "We had [[Michael Dunn (American football)|Michael Dunn]] step in at left guard for [[Joel Bitonio]]. And then, Michael got hurt and a guy named Blake, that I introduced myself to literally in the locker room before the game, stepped up in the fourth quarter."<ref>{{Cite web |last=DeArdo |first=Bryan |date=January 10, 2021 |title=Baker Mayfield introduced himself to replacement lineman in locker room prior to Browns' playoff win |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/baker-mayfield-introduced-himself-to-replacement-lineman-in-locker-room-prior-to-browns-playoff-win/ |access-date=January 11, 2021 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref>

The Browns placed an [[exclusive-rights free agent]] tender on Hance on March 7, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Poisal |first=Anthony |date=March 7, 2022 |title=Browns designate TE David Njoku as franchise player, tender three |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-designate-te-david-njoku-as-franchise-player-tender-three |access-date=March 8, 2022 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com}}</ref> Hance was waived by the Browns on August 30, 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Poisal |first=Anthony |date=August 30, 2022 |title=Browns announce initial 53-man roster heading into 2022 season |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-announce-initial-53-man-roster-heading-into-2022-season}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On August 31, 2022, Hance was claimed off waivers by the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 31, 2022 |title=49ers Move Two to IR; Waive RB; Announce Practice Squad and Other Moves |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/ir-ward-robinson-sermon-waive-rb-announce-practice-squad |access-date=January 28, 2023 |website=49ers.com}}</ref> He appeared in seven games with the 49ers, and was later waived on October 29.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Hance 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HancBl00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=March 13, 2025 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 29, 2022 |title=49ers Promote WR Snead IV to the Active Roster; Waive an Offensive Lineman |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-promote-wr-willie-snead-iv-waive-ol-blake-hance-elevate-martin-mcgill |access-date=January 28, 2023 |website=49ers.com}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars (second stint)===
On November 1, 2022, Hance was claimed off waivers by the Jaguars.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 1, 2022 |title=Roster Moves: Jaguars claim offensive lineman Blake Hance off of waivers |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-jaguars-claim-offensive-lineman-blake-hance-off-of-waivers |access-date=October 31, 2024 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref>

On August 27, 2024, Hance was released by the Jaguars and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Roster Moves: Jacksonville Jaguars Make The Following Roster Moves Hours Before 2024 Roster Deadline |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-jacksonville-jaguars-make-the-following-roster-moves-hours-before-2024-roster-deadline |access-date=October 31, 2024 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Roster Moves: Jaguars Sign OL Blake Hance, S Matthew Jackson and WR Louis Rees-Zammit to the Practice Squad |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-jaguars-sign-ol-blake-hance-s-matthew-jackson-and-wr-louis-rees-zammit-to-the-practice-squad |website=Jaguars.com |publisher=Jacksonville Jaguars |access-date=August 30, 2024}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 29.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 29, 2024 |title=Roster Moves: Jaguars Make Three Roster Moves Including Signing Blake Hance to 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/k000030-roster-moves-jaguars-make-three-roster-moves-including-signing-blake-hance-to-53-man-roster |access-date=October 31, 2024 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> 

Hance appeared in 35 games during his three seasons with the Jaguars.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Hance 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HancBl00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=March 13, 2025 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On March 13, 2025, Hance signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]] on a one-year, $1.3 million contract.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |website=TennesseeTitans.com |title=Titans Sign Offensive Lineman Blake Hance |date=March 13, 2025 |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-offensive-lineman-blake-hance |access-date=March 13, 2025}}</ref>

'''Blake Haubeil''' (born April 5, 1999)<ref name=birthday /> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[placekicker]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]] and was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Tennessee Titans|Titans]] after the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://buckeyeswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/buckeyes/football/2021/05/05/tennessee-titans-signed-ohio-state-blake-haubeil-as-undrafted-free-agent/78154381007/|first=Josh|last=Keatley|title=Tennessee Titans signed Blake Haubeil as undrafted free agent|website=Buckeyes Wire}}</ref>

==College career==
Haubeil was ranked as a three{{endash}}star recruit by [[247Sports.com]] coming out of high school.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Blake-Haubeil-84072/high-school-145589/|title=Blake Haubeil Recruiting Profile|website=247Sports.com}}</ref> He committed to [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State]] on July 24, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/player/blake-haubeil-84072/|title=Blake Haubeil 247|website=247Sports.com}}</ref>

'''Miles Bokeem Melton''' (born May 18, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] for the [[Green Bay Packers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]], and was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the seventh round of the [[2022 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Melton grew up in [[Mays Landing, New Jersey]] and attended [[Cedar Creek High School (New Jersey)|Cedar Creek High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fonseca |first=Brian |date=March 2, 2022 |title=NFL Combine 2022: Rutgers star Bo Melton will 'play anywhere' on field |url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersfootball/2022/03/nfl-combine-2022-rutgers-star-bo-melton-will-play-anywhere-on-field.html |access-date=April 7, 2022 |website=[[NJ.com]]}}</ref> As a senior, Melton caught 51 receptions for 766 yards and nine [[touchdowns]] and also rushed for 451 yards and seven touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Evans |first=Bill |date=February 1, 2017 |title=Bo Melton, Owen Bowles of Cedar Creek sign to play football for Rutgers on National Signing Day |url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersfootball/2017/02/bo_melton_owen_bowles_of_cedar_creek_sign_to_play.html |access-date=April 8, 2022 |website=[[NJ.com]]}}</ref> He was rated a four-star recruit and committed to play [[college football]] at Rutgers from over 30 scholarship offers, including Michigan, Ohio State, Oregon, Penn State, Virginia Tech, Wisconsin, Nebraska, Maryland, and Pitt.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McGarry |first=Michael |date=April 16, 2016 |title=Cedar Creek football star Bo Melton commits to Rutgers |url=https://pressofatlanticcity.com/sports/local/highschool/cedar-creek-football-star-bo-melton-commits-to-rutgers/article_9df3f1b0-036d-11e6-9a09-cfb2bafb5f2a.html |access-date=April 8, 2022 |website=[[The Press of Atlantic City]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hunt |first=Todderick |date=April 16, 2016 |title=4-star N.J. WR legacy Bo Melton stays home, commits to Rutgers |url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersfootball/2016/04/4-star_nj_wr_bo_melton_stays_home_commits_to_rutge.html |access-date=April 8, 2022 |website=[[NJ.com]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Melton played in 11 games as a freshman and had four receptions for 83 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nalwasky |first=Chris |date=July 19, 2018 |title=Breaking down Bo Melton's three-touchdown Scarlet-White game |url=https://rutgers.rivals.com/news/breaking-down-bo-melton-s-three-touchdown-scarlet-white-game/ |access-date=April 7, 2022 |website=[[Rivals.com]]}}</ref> He played in all 12 of Rutgers' games and caught 28 passes for 245 yards in his sophomore season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sargeant |first=Keith |date=April 9, 2019 |title=Why did Rutgers' wide receivers struggle last season? Lester Erb has an answer that should give fans hope for a big improvement in 2019 |url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersfootball/2019/04/why-did-rutgers-wide-receivers-struggle-last-season-lester-erb-has-an-answer-that-should-give-fans-hope-for-a-big-improvement-in-2019.html |access-date=April 7, 2022 |website=[[NJ.com]]}}</ref> As a junior, Melton led the Scarlet Knights with 30 receptions and 427 receiving yards and caught two touchdown passes.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sargeant |first=Keith |date=October 20, 2020 |title=Here's the stat that shows how valuable Bo Melton is to Rutgers' offense |url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersfootball/2020/10/heres-the-stat-that-shows-how-valuable-bo-melton-is-to-rutgers-offense.html |access-date=April 7, 2022 |website=[[NJ.com]]}}</ref> In 2020, he again led the team with 47 catches and 638 receiving yards with six touchdown receptions and also rushed for two touchdowns and scored on a punt return.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sargeant |first=Keith |date=October 2, 2021 |title=Rutgers loses to Ohio State: Bigger concern is injury to star wide receiver Bo Melton |url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersfootball/2021/10/rutgers-loses-to-ohio-state-bigger-concern-is-injury-to-star-wide-receiver-bo-melton.html |access-date=April 7, 2022 |website=[[NJ.com]]}}</ref> Melton decided to utilize the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes who played in the 2020 season due to the coronavirus pandemic and return to Rutgers for a fifth season. He caught a career high 55 passes for 618 yards and three touchdowns in his final season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stapleton |first=Art |date=March 3, 2022 |title=Bo Melton NFL Combine results: 40-yard dash times wow teams |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/nfl/giants/2022/03/03/rutgers-bo-melton-knows-nfl-combine-gridiron-dream/9349587002/ |access-date=April 7, 2022 |website=[[Asbury Park Press]]}}</ref> After the conclusion of his college career, Melton played in the [[2022 Senior Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zangaro |first=Dave |date=February 4, 2022 |title=Draft Journey: Rutgers' Melton impressing at Senior Bowl |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/eagles/nfl-draft-journey-rutgers-bo-melton-impressing-senior-bowl |access-date=April 7, 2022 |website=[[NBC Sports Philadelphia]]}}</ref>

|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-elevate-wr-bo-melton-and-s-benny-sapp-iii-for-gameday-week-16 |website=Packers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 30, 2023 |title=Packers sign S Benny Sapp III to active roster |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-s-benny-sapp-iii-to-active-roster-week-17-2023 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> On December 31, he had a breakout game against the [[2023 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]] with six receptions for 105 yards and a touchdown.<ref name="o744">{{cite web | last=Hodkiewicz | first=Wes | title=Game notes: Bo Melton’s perseverance rewarded with first NFL TD, 100-yard day | website=Packers.com| date=January 1, 2024 | url=https://www.packers.com/news/game-notes-bo-melton-s-perseverance-rewarded-with-first-nfl-td-100-yard-day | access-date=November 3, 2024}}</ref> Melton was signed to the active roster the following day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 1, 2024 |title=Packers sign WR Bo Melton to active roster |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-wr-bo-melton-to-active-roster-230101 |access-date=January 1, 2024 |website=Packers.com}}</ref>

In the Packers' divisional round matchup against the [[2023 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]], Melton caught his only target for a 19-yard touchdown reception.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Easterling |first=Luke |date=January 20, 2024 |title=7th-Round Steal Bo Melton Making a Splash for Packers |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/draft/news/nfl-playoffs-green-bay-packers-bo-melton-nfl-draft |access-date=July 19, 2024 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref>

Prior to the [[2025 NFL season]], the Packers converted Melton into a [[cornerback]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Packers CB Bo Melton's position change is paying off with coaches|url=https://packerswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/packers/2025/07/30/packers-cb-bo-meltons-position-change-is-paying-off-with-coaches/85446282007/|access-date=July 30, 2025|website=packerswire.usatoday.com|language=en}}</ref> He made 16 appearances (one start) for Green Bay, recording four receptions for 107 yards and a touchdown; he also recorded four combined tackles. On January 7, 2026, Melton was placed on season-ending injured reserve due to a knee injury suffered in Week 18 against the [[2025 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Packers activate LB Nick Niemann off injured reserve|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-activate-lb-nick-niemann-off-injured-reserve-jan-7-2026|access-date=January 22, 2026|website=packers.com|language=en}}</ref>

On June 2, 2026, it was announced that Melton would go back to playing wide receiver full-time.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Packers change Bo Melton's position back to WR to start OTAs|url=https://packerswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/packers/2026/05/28/packers-change-bo-meltons-position-back-to-wr-to-start-otas/90292293007/|access-date=June 16, 2026|website=packerswire.usatoday.com|language=en}}</ref>

'''Blake Freeland''' (born May 3, 2001) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[BYU Cougars football|BYU Cougars]].

==Early life and college==
Freeland was born in [[Herriman, Utah]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 13, 2023 |title=NFL Draft Profile: Blake Freeland, Offensive Lineman, BYU Cougars |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/draft/news/blakefreeland |access-date=March 5, 2023 |website=SI.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-04 |title=Blake Freeland: Indianapolis Colts Rookie Files |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/colts/news/blake-freeland-colts-offensive-tackle-rookie-files |access-date=2025-07-29 |website=Indianapolis Colts On SI |language=en-US}}</ref> He played football at [[Herriman High School]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ireland |first=Kyle |date=2023-04-29 |title=Former BYU OL Blake Freeland Selected In 2023 NFL Draft |url=https://kslsports.com/local-athletes/locals-in-nfl/former-byu-offensive-tackle-blake-freeland-selected-2023-nfl-draft/500646 |access-date=2025-07-29 |website=KSL Sports |language=en-us}}</ref> where he played [[quarterback]] his sophomore and junior year and [[tight end]] and [[defensive end]] as a senior.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Drew |first=Jay |date=November 19, 2019 |title=Blake Freeland was a 6-foot-8 quarterback in high school. Now the true freshman is starting on BYU’s offensive line |url=https://www.deseret.com/2019/11/19/20972515/blake-freeland-was-a-qb-in-high-school-now-the-true-freshman-is-starting-byu-offensive-line |access-date=March 5, 2023 |website=Deseret.com}}</ref> Freeland then attended [[Brigham Young University]], where he played [[college football]] for the [[BYU Cougars football|Cougars]] from 2019 to 2022.

==Professional career==
Freeland holds an [[NFL Combine]] record for an offensive lineman with a 37" [[vertical jump]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lundquist |first=Casey |date=March 5, 2023 |title=BYU Offensive Lineman Blake Freeland Sets New Vertical Jump Record at NFL Combine |url=https://www.si.com/college/byu/cougars-in-the-pros/byu-offensive-lineman-blake-freeland-sets-new-vertical-jump-record-at-nfl-combine |access-date=March 5, 2023 |website=SI.com}}</ref>

Freeland was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the fourth round, 106th overall, of the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stankevitz |first=JJ |date=April 29, 2023 |title=Colts select BYU offensive tackle Blake Freeland with No. 106 pick in 2023 NFL Draft |url=https://www.colts.com/news/2023-nfl-draft-pick-fourth-round-blake-freeland-tackle-byu |access-date=June 28, 2023 |website=Colts.com}}</ref> He started his first NFL game on October 1, 2023, following an injury to Colts starting left tackle [[Bernhard Raimann]]. After two starts at left tackle, he started seven of the final 12 games at right tackle in place of an injured [[Braden Smith (American football)|Braden Smith]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blake Freeland 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FreeBl00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-07-28 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On August 18, 2025, Freeland was placed on season-ending injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts sign CB Xavien Howard; place T Blake Freeland, LB Jacob Phillips, S Hunter Wohler on injured reserve|url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-cb-xavien-howard-place-t-blake-freeland-lb-jacob-phillips-s-hunter-wohler-on-injured-reserve|author=Stankevitz, JJ|website=Colts.com|date=August 18, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Freeland's father, Jim, played linebacker at BYU in the 1990s.  Freeland’s mother, Debbie (Diamond) Freeland, played Basketball and Volleyball at BYU in the 1990’s. <ref>{{Cite web |last=Drew |first=Jay |date=September 23, 2021 |title=Leaving a legacy: 17 players on the BYU football team have fathers who also played for Cougars |url=https://www.deseret.com/2021/9/23/22671606/byu-football-has-17-legacy-players-cougars-whose-fathers-also-played-for-byu-jaren-hall-isaac-rex |access-date=March 5, 2023 |website=Deseret.com}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]].

==Early life==
Fisher attended and played [[high school football]] at [[Avon High School (Indiana)|Avon High School]] in [[Avon, Indiana]]. After his senior season, he was named Mr. Football Indiana for offensive line and earned IFCA First Team All-State.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Neddenriep |first=Kyle |date=December 7, 2020 |title=Here are the 2020 Mr. Football position award winners named by IFCA |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/12/07/indiana-high-school-football-2020-mr-football-position-award-winners-blake-fisher-carson-steele/6477814002/ |website=IndyStar}}</ref> Fisher committed to the [[University of Notre Dame]] to play college football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Neddenriep |first=Kyle |date=June 21, 2019 |title=Football recruiting notebook: Avon four-star Blake Fisher all-in on Notre Dame |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/06/21/indiana-high-school-football-recruiting-blake-fisher-picks-notre-dame/1525520001/ |access-date=May 26, 2024 |website=IndyStar}}</ref>

==College career==
As a true freshman at Notre Dame in 2021, Fisher won the starting left tackle position. He went down with a knee injury in the first game of the season against [[Florida State Seminoles football|Florida State]] and returned at the end of the season for the [[2022 Fiesta Bowl (January)|bowl game]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Driskell |first=Bryan |date=June 5, 2023 |title=Notre Dame Lineman Blake Fisher Is Poised For A Breakout Season |url=https://www.si.com/college/notredame/football/notre-dame-football-lineman-blake-fisher-is-poised-for-a-breakout-season |access-date=May 26, 2024 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> In 2022, Fisher started all 13 games at right tackle.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://und.com/roster/blake-fisher/|title=Blake Fisher – Notre Dame Fighting Irish|website=und.com|date=December 13, 2020 }}</ref>

He later was a coach. ==Early life== Miller was born on August 23, 1968, in [[Alexandria, Louisiana]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MillBl21.htm|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|title=Blake Miller Stats}} He attended [[Alexandria Senior High School]], where he won two [[varsity letter]]s and was a starting [[offensive tackle]] and [[long snapper]].{{Cite web|url=https://lsusports.net/sports/fb/roster/player/blake-miller/|publisher=[[LSU Tigers]]|title=Blake Miller}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-town-talk/145254455/|newspaper=[[The Town Talk]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=November 7, 1985|page=15|title=Pow-Wow Helps Unite ASH Offense|author=D'Aquila, John}} {{Open access}} As a [[Senior (education)|senior]], he was named first-team Class AAAA All-State.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-town-talk/145254712/|newspaper=[[The Town Talk]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 6, 1988|page=11, [https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-town-talk/145254809/ 15]|title=Miller's time at LSU|author=Ireland, Doug}} {{Open access}} He was named one of the top 24 recruits in the state by the ''[[Baton Rouge Morning Advocate]]'' and committed to play [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]] over a number of other offers. ==College career== Miller noted that he arrived at LSU in poor shape and "didn't know what hard work was." He initially performed poorly in school and had difficulty listening to the coaches. However, he then was told by coach [[Pete Mangurian]] that "You're never going to play if you don't learn how to work," and Miller became motivated to improve, starting a "turnaround" with him improving his grades and getting in better shape. Considered small for tackle at {{convert|6|ft|2|in}} and {{convert|250|lb|kg}}, he moved to [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] and also practiced at [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] as a [[freshman]] in 1986. He [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] that year. In spring practice prior to the 1987 season, Miller began as the first-team center due to injuries to several others at the position.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-town-talk/145256339/|newspaper=[[The Town Talk]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=April 4, 1987|page=11, [https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-town-talk/145256427/ 14]|title=Alexandria's Miller Becomes The 'Center' of Attention|author=Tompkins, Bob}} {{Open access}} He ultimately returned to guard before the season began and played in 10 games as a backup, also serving as backup center but not seeing any action in that role. He helped them reach the [[1987 Gator Bowl]], where the Tigers defeated the [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina Gamecocks]]. Miller moved permanently to center prior to the 1988 season and became a backup to Todd Coutee. He ultimately played in seven games that season, which included a start against the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]] when Coutee was injured. After Coutee graduated in 1989, Miller became LSU's full-time starter at center.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-town-talk/145256863/|newspaper=[[The Town Talk]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 31, 1989|page=59|title=Blake Miller ready to fill center slot at LSU|author=Guilbeau, Glenn}} {{Open access}} He started all but one of the team's games and helped them reach a bowl game.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/southwest-daily-news/145256943/|newspaper=[[Southwest Daily News]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 18, 1990|page=11|agency=[[Associated Press]]|title=Center Blake Miller is the leader of LSU's young line}} {{Open access}} He entered the 1990 season as the team's only returning starter from the 1986 class.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-town-talk/145256990/|newspaper=[[The Town Talk]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 5, 1990|page=17, [https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-town-talk/145257054/ 22]|title=The lonely guy|author=Guilbeau, Glenn}} {{Open access}} He started all 11 games in the 1990 season and blocked for future first-round [[NFL draft]] pick [[Harvey Williams (American football)|Harvey Williams]], earning [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) honors from the league's coaches and second-team honors from the [[Associated Press]] (AP). He was invited to the [[Blue–Gray Football Classic]], the [[East–West Shrine Bowl]], and the [[NFL Scouting Combine]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-town-talk/145257338/|newspaper=[[The Town Talk]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=January 26, 1991|page=9|title=Miller thinks it's important he shine in Shrine|author=Guilbeau, Glenn}} {{Open access}} He graduated from LSU with a [[bachelor's degree]] in general studies and ended his college football career having been twice named the Tigers' offensive lineman of the year.{{Cite web|url=https://gotigersgo.com/news/2011/1/20/Utah_s_Blake_Miller_Added_To_Tiger_Football_Staff|publisher=[[Memphis Tigers]]|title=Utah's Blake Miller Added To Tiger Football Staff|date=January 20, 2011}} ==Professional career== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 1 3/8 | weight = 281 | dash = 5.14 | ten split = 1.79 | twenty split = 2.96 | shuttle = 4.55 | vertical = 28.5 | broad ft = 9 | broad in = 1 | bench = 21 | arm span = 32 | hand span = 10 1/4 }} Miller was selected in the seventh round (168th overall) of the [[1991 NFL draft]] by the [[New England Patriots]]. He was released as part of the team's final roster cuts.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-boston-globe/145257514/|newspaper=[[The Boston Globe]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 27, 1991|page=26|author=Borges, Ron|title=Roster is down to size}} {{Open access}} He was re-signed to the team on their [[practice squad]] shortly after.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/hartford-courant/145257577/|newspaper=[[Hartford Courant]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 29, 1991|page=142|title=Transactions}} {{Open access}} He appeared in no games for the team and became a [[free agent]] after the season.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/lansing-state-journal/145257639/|newspaper=[[Lansing State Journal]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=April 11, 1992|page=14|title=Michigan}} {{Open access}} Miller was signed by the [[Detroit Lions]] in April 1992. He started in preseason and ultimately made the final roster.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-town-talk/145257842/|newspaper=[[The Town Talk]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 23, 1992|page=23|title=Former LSU center makes headway with NFL's Lions|author=Guilbeau, Glenn}} {{Open access}} Initially a backup, he saw action as a starter following an injury to [[Kevin Glover]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/detroit-free-press/145258001/|newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 27, 1992|page=95|title=Lions must defy injuries, go on another big streak|author=Sylvester, Curt}} {{Open access}} His season ended in mid-December when he was placed on [[injured reserve]] as a result of a sprained ankle.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/detroit-free-press/145258038/|newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=December 17, 1992|page=74|title=Notebook}} {{Open access}} He appeared in a total of 14 games, five as a starter, during the 1992 season for the Lions. He was [[Waivers (NFL)|waived]] by the Lions in early May 1993 and was then claimed by the [[New York Giants]], although they later released him in August 1993, ending his playing career.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/fort-worth-star-telegram/145258142/|newspaper=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=May 18, 1993|page=35|title=Pro Football}} {{Open access}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/hartford-courant/145258201/|newspaper=[[Hartford Courant]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 24, 1993|page=24|title=NFL transactions}} {{Open access}} ==Coaching career== Miller began coaching after his playing career, assisting at the [[Episcopal School of Baton Rouge]] and [[Kilgore High School]] between 1994 and 1996. He then joined the [[Northwestern State Demons football|Northwestern State Demons]] and was their offensive line coach from 1997 to 1999, helping them win two conference championships. He then joined the [[Texas State Bobcats football|Southwest Texas State Bobcats]] as offensive line coach in 2000 and rose to [[offensive coordinator]] in 2001. He joined the [[SMU Mustangs football|SMU Mustangs]] as offensive line coach in 2003 before returning to the Bobcats in 2004, serving the next three seasons as offensive line coach and co-offensive coordinator.{{Cite web|url=https://www.ksl.com/article/5552176/blake-miller-is-new-ute-o-line-coach?comments=true|website=[[KSL.com]]|title=Blake Miller is new Ute O-Line coach|date=February 9, 2009}} He left for the [[Rice Owls football|Rice Owls]] in 2007 and served two seasons as run game coordinator and offensive line coach, helping them win 10 games with a [[2008 Texas Bowl]] win in his second year.{{Cite news|url=https://www.deseret.com/2009/2/10/20301182/utah-utes-football-utah-hires-rice-s-miller-to-coach-o-line/|newspaper=[[Deseret News]]|title=Utah Utes football: Utah hires Rice's Miller to coach O-line|date=February 10, 2009|author=Facer, Dirk}} Miller became the offensive line coach for the [[Utah Utes football|Utah Utes]] in 2009 and, after two seasons there, left for the same role with the [[Memphis Tigers football|Memphis Tigers]] in 2011.{{Cite news|url=https://www.victoriaadvocate.com/news/business/miller-joins-memphis-staff-as-offensive-line-coach/article_4af914a8-8bcb-5845-b2d4-56a4da0c0bbe.html|newspaper=[[The Victoria Advocate]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|title=Miller joins Memphis staff as offensive line coach|date=January 10, 2011}} He was not retained after his first season at Memphis.{{Cite news|url=https://sports.usatoday.com/ncaa/salaries/football/assistant/190|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|title=Memphis Coach Blake Miller Salary}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Patriots1991DraftPicks}} '''Bo Richter''' (born August 13, 2000)<ref name=birthday>{{cite web|url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/player/53750/|title=Bo Richter|website=ourlads.com|access-date=August 19, 2024}}</ref> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Minnesota Vikings]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Air Force Falcons football|Air Force Falcons]].

== Early life ==
Richter attended [[Naperville North High School]] located in [[Naperville, Illinois]]. Coming out of high school, Richter committed to play [[college football]] for the [[Air Force Falcons football|Air Force Falcons]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bo Richter - Recruiting Profile |url=https://www.on3.com/db/bo-richter-11190/recruiting/ |website=On3.com |access-date=23 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Naperville North's Big Time Edge Rusher Bo Richter Talks Recruiting |url=https://www.deepdishfootball.com/single-post/2018/07/01/naperville-norths-big-time-edge-rusher-bo-richter-talks-recruiting-camps-huskie-football |website=Deep Dish Football |date=1 July 2018 |access-date=23 August 2024}}</ref>

== College career ==
During Richter's first two seasons in 2019, and 2020, he did not appear in any games for the Falcons.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bo Richter - Football |url=https://goairforcefalcons.com/sports/football/roster/bo-richter/12332 |website=Air Force Academy Athletics |access-date=23 August 2024}}</ref> In the [[2021 First Responder Bowl]], Richter notched three tackles, with half of one being for a loss, in a victory over [[2021 Louisville Cardinals football team|Louisville]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Briggeman |first1=Brent |title=Position change for linebacker Bo Richter has boosted Air Force's defense |url=https://gazette.com/sports/position-change-for-linebacker-bo-richter-has-boosted-air-forces-defense/article_7da5436e-451f-11ed-bb4e-37282e272685.html |website=Colorado Springs Gazette |date=6 October 2022 |access-date=23 August 2024}}</ref> Richter finished the 2021 season tallying 13 tackles with one and a half being for a loss, a sack and a half, a pass deflection, and an interception.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Forness |first1=Tyler |title=Will Bo Richter's athleticism catapult him to a roster spot? |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/minnesota-vikings/news/minnesota-vikings-90-man-roster-bo-richter-athleticism/930312f99a87a8f4edcf3ce1 |website=Sporting News |date=9 June 2024 |access-date=23 August 2024}}</ref> In the 2022 season, Richter totaled 26 tackles with five and a half going for a loss.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Briggeman |first1=Brent |title=Trey Taylor, Bo Richter among Air Force football players working out at Pro Day |url=https://gazette.com/sports/trey-taylor-bo-richter-among-air-force-football-players-working-out-at-pro-day/article_0a5670c2-e1a9-11ee-800e-f34a39ffa587.html |website=Colorado Springs Gazette |date=13 March 2024 |access-date=23 August 2024}}</ref> During Richter's final collegiate game in the [[2023 Armed Forces Bowl]], Richter totaled four and a half tackles for a loss, and three sacks, as he helped Air Force to a win over [[2023 James Madison Dukes football team|James Madison]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Briggeman |first1=Brent |title=Bo Richter wows as he shared NFL preseason debut stage with Trey Taylor |url=https://gazette.com/sports/air-force-notebook-bo-richter-wows-as-he-shared-nfl-preseason-debut-stage-with-trey/article_20035b72-577b-11ef-b588-6f036d294d2f.html |website=Colorado Springs Gazette |date=10 August 2024 |access-date=23 August 2024}}</ref> Richter finished the 2023 season recording 45 tackles with 19.5 being for a loss, ten sacks, and three forced fumbles, en route to being named first-team all-Mountain West.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kleifield |first=Rob |date=August 15, 2024 |title=Bo Richter's Non-Stop Motor Helped His Take-off at Air Force & Vikings Debut |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/bo-richter-rookie-outside-linebacker-air-force-vikings-debut |access-date=23 August 2024 |website=Minnesota Vikings}}</ref>

After not being selected in the [[2024 NFL draft]], Richter signed with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] as an [[undrafted free agent]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Ragatz |first1=Will |title=Undrafted Vikings OLB Bo Richter is a crazy athlete and a potential steal |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/vikings/news/undrafted-vikings-olb-bo-richter-is-a-crazy-athlete-and-a-potential-steal-01j58x2k1w30 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |access-date=23 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Briggeman |first1=Brent |title=Air Force's Bo Richter, Alec Mock sign with NFL teams as undrafted free agents |url=https://gazette.com/sports/air-forces-bo-richter-alec-mock-sign-with-nfl-teams-as-undrafted-free-agents/article_236d4660-04fb-11ef-a93a-6faca04d95f4.html |website=Colorado Springs Gazette |date=27 April 2024 |access-date=23 August 2024}}</ref> Richter was also selected in the sixth round of the [[2024 UFL draft]] by the [[Arlington Renegades]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ryan |first=Chris |date=17 July 2024 |title=Air Force's Richter selected by UFL's Renegades |url=https://www.fox21news.com/sports/air-forces-richter-selected-by-ufls-renegades/ |access-date=23 August 2024 |website=Fox21}}</ref> He was waived on August 27, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Utilize Reserve Lists During Roster Cuts: T.J. Hockenson on Reserve/PUP|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-utilize-reserve-lists-during-roster-cuts-t-j-hockenson-on-reserve-pup|author=Peters, Craig|website=Vikings.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Sign 17 Players to 2024 Practice Squad|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/2024-practice-squad-sign-17-players|author=Peters, Craig|website=Vikings.com|date=August 28, 2024}}</ref> He was signed to the active roster on October 22, 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vikings Sign Bo Richter to Active Roster from Practice Squad; Terminate Contract of Robert Tonyan |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/bo-richter-signed-active-roster-robert-tonyan-contract-terminated-roster-moves |last1=Young |first1=Lindsey |website=Vikings.com |date=October 22, 2024}}</ref>

On March 9, 2026, Richter re-signed with the Vikings.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kleffield |first1=Rob |date=March 9, 2026 |title=Vikings Re-Sign Bo Richter & Zavier Scott |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/bo-richter-zavier-scott-re-sign-contract-2026-nfl |access-date=10 March 2026 |website=vikings.com}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Richter is the nephew of former [[New York Giants]] quarterback, [[Kent Graham]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lewis |first1=Alec |title=Vikings UDFA signings: 17 thoughts on the 17 post-NFL Draft additions |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5455946/2024/04/29/vikings-nfl-draft-udfa-signings/ |date=29 April 2024 |access-date=23 August 2024}}</ref>
